title: He sang… when they were already drifting.
paragraphs: He sang… when they were already drifting.

Not when they rebelled loudly.
Not when they built idols in public.
But when their hearts were quietly… leaving.
And that’s what makes this terrifying.

Because you can look faithful—
and already be gone.
Moses stood there, old, worn, eyes burning with truth, and he sang a warning Israel didn’t feel they needed.
“Jeshurun grew fat and kicked… he abandoned the God who made him” (Deuteronomy 32:15).

They didn’t walk away in weakness.
They walked away in comfort.

What if your greatest spiritual danger…
is not your struggle—

What if the prayers God answered
became the very reason you stopped depending on Him?
We don’t like to admit this.

But some of us didn’t drift in rebellion.
We drifted in routine.

Still attending.
Still posting verses.
Still saying “God is good.”

You don’t hate God—
you just don’t hunger for Him anymore.
And that scares heaven more than your worst mistake.
Moses saw it before it happened.
“You will forget the Rock who gave you birth” (Deuteronomy 32:18).
Delayed obedience that felt harmless at first.

That “one thing” God told you to surrender…
but you kept negotiating.

That quiet pride that whispers,
“I’m still better than others.”
That spiritual fatigue you hide behind busyness.

When was the last time you obeyed God
without hesitation?

When was the last time His Word cut you…
and you didn’t explain it away?
Here’s the part we don’t preach enough:
God’s judgment in Deuteronomy 32 isn’t random.
“They provoked Him to jealousy with foreign gods” (Deuteronomy 32:16).
The kind of love that refuses to share your heart with idols.

Because every idol promises life—
but slowly drains it.

And God will let you feel the emptiness
of what you chose over Him.
This is where it gets personal.

Some of you aren’t in open sin—
but you’re in quiet replacement.

And you’re wondering why your soul feels dry
even when your life looks full.

You don’t lose God in a moment—
you replace Him in layers.

The thing you run to for comfort
is revealing who you trust as your savior.

Right in the middle of warning—
God speaks something shocking:
“The Lord will vindicate His people and have compassion on His servants” (Deuteronomy 32:36).

Because God’s justice is real—
but His mercy runs deeper.
But here’s the line that should shake you:
“See now that I, even I, am He, and there is no god besides Me” (Deuteronomy 32:39).
And this is where the song points forward.
Because Deuteronomy 32 ends with a word that echoes into eternity:
“He will atone for His land and His people” (Deuteronomy 32:43).

Where Israel forgot—He remained faithful.
Where we drift—He stands firm.

You and I deserved the fire described in that song.
The consequences.
The separation.
“He was pierced for our transgressions… the punishment that brought us peace was on Him” (Isaiah 53:5).

You sinned.
Not just in actions—
but in affection.
On the cross, He absorbed the judgment Moses warned about.
Here’s the conviction you didn’t expect:

You can sing worship songs
and still be living a slow goodbye to God.
But here’s the hope you desperately need:
You can come back… right now.
You are not just someone trying to “do better.”
You are called to be a person who belongs to the Rock.
but because Jesus never let go.
Say it—even if your voice shakes:
Not information—transformation. Quiet time with God that actually changes you.
If this pierced you, don’t ignore it.
And the next message might be the one your soul has been waiting for.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
